source.title: Spectral phase transitions and trainability in neural network learning dynamics
source.authors: Chanju Park; Dario Bocchi; Francesco D'Amico; B. Lucini; Gert Aarts

record.file_problem: Full text supplied, including appendices; no truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies gradient-training dynamics and how learning rate and initialization affect trainability, but it measures spectral alignment and test loss rather than benchmark training classification error. Those results conceptually bear on V1 and V4.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own results on spectral alignment and realistic-data test loss. It does not report CIFAR classification training error, random-label fitting, or the depth/shortcut comparisons in V1–V3. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures spectral alignment and final regression test loss as learning rate and initial variance vary. These do not test V4's activation-matched initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth. Its linear convergence analysis also does not test V5: convergence for 1 < ε < 2 remains below the quadratic model's stability limit, without a catapult or evolving curvature.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose dynamical BBP transitions as an organizing framework for spectral representation formation, derive exact linear teacher-student dynamics, and report qualitative extensions to nonlinear networks and UTKFace regression. They acknowledge that practical universality remains unresolved and nonlinear/multilayer theory mainly covers the first update and first layer.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies full-batch gradient descent in a solvable teacher-student model, then SGD on UTKFace age regression; it measures spectral overlap and test loss rather than classification training error. No CIFAR experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Step size, initial weight variance, activation (linear, tanh, ReLU), finite-data load parameter, architecture depth, and training time affect the reported phase or alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning rate and initial variance control the emergence and persistence of teacher-aligned spectral modes in linear, tanh and ReLU models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient updates can induce a dynamical BBP transition whose boundaries depend on learning rate, initial variance and activation.

fits_no_version.finding: Shallow and three-hidden-layer UTKFace regressors achieve lower final test loss within an intermediate region of learning rates and initial variances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Final age-regression generalization performance depends jointly on learning rate and initial weight variance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across training seeds, first-layer subspaces remain random in disordered regimes, align in leading PCA directions in paramagnetic regimes, and share broader subspaces in ferromagnetic regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different optimization regimes produce distinct forms of first-layer spectral alignment and representation structure.

record.code_released: The code and data used for the manuscript are stated to be made available in v2 of the arXiv version; no URL stated.
record.problems: Realistic experiments use UTKFace age regression and report test loss rather than training classification error. Most phase-diagram outcomes are shown only in figures without tabulated numeric values. Nonlinear and multilayer theory is largely restricted to the first optimization step and first layer; the paper itself says practical universality remains unclear.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Cited findings from other papers were not extracted as this study's results.

untested.parts: CIFAR convolutional-network training classification error, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe effects.
Spurious local-minimum frequency as teacher/student widths grow and the benefit of extra student neurons.
Depth-related training-error degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization preserving propagation across layers; training-speed and trainable-depth comparisons; orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization; very deep convolutional training.
Above-stability-limit recovery, transient loss growth with curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from initially subthreshold rates.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V4 limits_scope verdict: dependence on hyperparameters and spectral alignment does not qualify a claim about activation-matched initialization improving training speed and depth. The study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 classification training error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, early stopping and regularization.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student spurious minima and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, training error by depth, shortcut effects, and the cited special initialization or normalization-free recipes.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, loss spikes and recovery, sharpness at the stability threshold, and divergence rates.
Batch normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup performance relative to normalization.

rows.subject: linear teacher-student model
rows.size_stated: N = 100 with aspect ratio r = 0.5 for numerical experiments in Sec. II C
rows.operation_detail: Varied step size at fixed initial randomness and measured squared overlap after one update.
rows.measure: Squared overlap q² between signal vector and top eigenvector
rows.note: The figure shows overlap by step size, but the prose does not give numeric values for this condition.
rows.check: Spectral overlap cannot establish V4. The value is not wholly unreadable: Fig. 4 explicitly states q² = 1 at ε = 1.

rows.subject: linear teacher-student model
rows.operation_detail: Measured squared overlap after 25 iterations over step size and initial randomness.
rows.note: Text says overlap in the paramagnetic region decreases as training proceeds and the phase boundary shifts; the figure does not report pointwise values.
rows.check: Overlap after 25 updates measures spectral alignment, not initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth.

rows.subject: hyperbolic tangent activation teacher-student model
rows.operation_detail: Compared squared-overlap phase diagrams after a first step and 75 iterations across step size and initial variance.
rows.note: Authors state the phase boundaries remain informative after 75 iterations and spurious paramagnetic overlap reduces.
rows.check: Tanh spectral phase diagrams do not compare activation-matched initialization recipes or measure training speed and depth.

rows.subject: ReLU activation teacher-student model
rows.operation_detail: Compared squared-overlap phase diagrams after a first step and 75 iterations across step size and initial variance.
rows.note: Authors state the initial overlap above the optimal boundary diminishes as training proceeds.
rows.check: ReLU spectral phase diagrams do not measure V4's training-speed or trainable-depth effects.

rows.subject: single-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Varied step size and initial variance and measured final test MAE on UTKFace.
rows.note: The authors say only a specific set of step sizes and initial variances near the figure's centre are well trained; values are not tabulated. This is a regression test-loss result, not training error.
rows.check: Final held-out age-prediction MAE after 300 epochs does not measure training speed or trainable depth. The subject is a fully connected network trained on real data.

rows.subject: single-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-k subspace self-overlap across phases during training.
rows.note: Text explicitly says the disordered phase follows qk ∼ k/D for all k, indicating no subspace alignment.
rows.check: Random-baseline subspace overlap establishes absent spectral alignment, not absent V4 effects.

rows.subject: single-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-k subspace self-overlap across phases during training.
rows.note: The leading direction aligns across samples, while higher-order directions remain uncorrelated.
rows.check: Alignment restricted to leading PCA directions is a representation result, not partial evidence for V4.

rows.subject: single-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-k subspace self-overlap across phases during training.
rows.note: Text describes substantial overlap over an extended range of k, indicating shared signal subspace.
rows.check: Shared spectral subspaces do not establish V4's initialization effects on speed or depth.

rows.subject: three-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Varied step size and initial variance and measured final test loss.
rows.note: Authors describe a qualitatively similar phase diagram to the shallow network, with successful learning only in an intermediate region.
rows.check: Final regression test loss does not establish initialization-dependent training speed or a depth limit. The subject is a fully connected network trained on real data.

rows.subject: three-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-k self-overlap of the first-layer weight matrix across phases.
rows.note: Text says overlap remains close to random-subspace expectation, indicating no coherent spectral alignment.
rows.check: First-layer spectral alignment near the random baseline cannot establish absence of V4's effect.

rows.subject: three-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-k self-overlap of the first-layer weight matrix across phases.
rows.note: Text says alignment is dominated by a small number of leading directions, reflecting a PCA representation.
rows.check: Leading-direction PCA alignment does not measure V4's effect.

rows.subject: three-hidden-layer ReLU network
rows.operation_detail: Measured top-k self-overlap of the first-layer weight matrix across phases.
rows.note: Text describes substantial and progressively growing subspace alignment.
rows.check: Growing first-layer subspace alignment does not establish faster training or greater trainable depth.
